edges.description: Reduced SNAP29 in patient skin is accompanied by abnormal maturation of the lamellar granules, the secretory organelles of the granular layer.
SNAP29 also serves autophagic fusion. Knockout mouse epidermis accumulates LC3B-II with unchanged p62/SQSTM1, the pattern expected when autophagosomes form but are not cleared.
Mislocated lipids and proteases leave the cornified envelope improperly formed, and the barrier fails.

nodes.description: The founding allele, homozygous in all patients of two large consanguineous families identified by homozygosity mapping.

Keratinocyte differentiation is abnormal and proliferation is increased, giving acanthosis and hyperkeratosis, and the epidermal barrier is severely impaired. In the mouse the phenotype is severe enough to be lethal in the neonatal period, which human patients survive — a species difference worth holding in mind when reading the mouse data.

nodes.description: SNAP29 participates in the fusion of autophagosomes with lysosomes. Its loss in mouse epidermis raises LC3B-II while leaving p62/SQSTM1 unchanged, and induces CHOP. This branch is the reason CEDNIK is discussed alongside the autophagy disorders, but note the whole of the evidence for it is murine.

nodes.description: Lamellar granules are the keratinocyte organelles that deliver barrier lipids and processing proteases into the intercellular space at the granular-to-cornified transition. Without SNAP29 they do not mature, and their cargo is mislocated. This is the specific lesion that makes CEDNIK an ichthyosis rather than a generic trafficking disease.

nodes.description: Epidermis and neural tissue share an embryonic origin, and the founding report framed CEDNIK as evidence that vesicle trafficking is required for proper neuroectodermal differentiation — which is the argument that the cutaneous and cerebral halves of this syndrome are one lesion rather than two. What the trafficking defect does in the developing brain is not resolved at the cellular level in any located source; the malformations are the observation, not the mechanism.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish SNAP29, a SNARE-family protein encoded at 22q11.2 and required for vesicle fusion. Patient skin shows decreased SNAP29 expression, and transfection experiments confirm that the reported variants are loss of function rather than altered function. Because SNAP29 acts at fusion steps used by more than one pathway, a single loss propagates into two separable downstream branches.

nodes.description: A loss-of-function line on a mixed background that reproduces the neurological and ophthalmological features as well as the skin, and so is the model for the half of the syndrome the keratinocyte-specific line cannot address. It also revealed a requirement for Snap29 in male fertility that has no reported human counterpart.

Total and keratinocyte-restricted knockouts, both giving a congenital ichthyotic phenotype with neonatal lethality. The keratinocyte-specific line is the informative one for the cutaneous arm: restricting the deletion to keratinocytes is sufficient to produce the skin disease.

A homozygous insertion reported in two sibs with ichthyosis and corpus callosum dysgenesis, shown by transfection to be loss of function. Reported elsewhere as c.486_487insA, where homozygotes may present with the full syndrome or with the neurological features alone.
